..
Issued at 300 AM EDT Thu Aug 13 2026

Currently-Tonight... KMLB radar imagery shows dry weather over
east central Florida. GOES-19 and local observations indicate
mostly clear to partly cloudy skies. Temperatures are currently in
the mid 70s to around 80 degrees with dew points in the low to mid
70s. Analysis charts show a mid/upper level ridge over the Gulf
and eastern CONUS. High pressure (1018mb) at the surface over the
eastern Gulf. Additionally, the 15Z and 00Z XMR skew-t soundings 
from yesterday still showed quite a bit of dry air in the mid to 
upper levels due to a Saharan Dust layer. 

Not much change is expected today in terms of the airmass with 
drier air still expected in the mid to upper levels due to Saharan
dust as high pressure builds over the Gulf and southern US. 
Isolated to scattered showers (30-50% chance) and lightning storms
are forecast to develop in the afternoon and evening today as 
collisions occur between light west-northwest flow, the east coast
sea breeze, and outflow from previous storms. Rain chances 
diminish by around 8PM. Light west- northwest winds will back 
onshore into the afternoon and evening as the east coast sea 
breeze pushes inland, mainly along and south of I-4. Hi-res 
guidance shows MLCAPE up to 1,000-3,600 J/kg, 0-6km shear up to 
10-25kts, PWATs up to 1.80-2.20", and mid level lapse rates up to 
6.0-6.7 C/km today. The aforementioned weather parameters are 
favorable for isolated strong storms capable of frequent 
lightning, wind gusts up to 30-50mph, and heavy rainfall (up to 
1-3"). Guidance shows 500mb heights at the 90th percentile (594dm)
and potentially the maximum percentile (597dm) by this evening 
over the southern US and the state of Florida. Thus, a hot and
muggy day is expected again with maximum temperatures in the mid
to upper 90s. Additionally, a Heat Advisory has been issued for 
all of east central Florida from 10AM to 8PM for heat index values
up to 108-112F degrees. Remember to take frequent breaks from the
heat, drink plenty of fluids, wear light colored clothing, and 
shift outdoor work away from the hottest parts of the day between 
the hours of 10am to 4pm. Above normal (2-4+ degrees) lows in mid
70s to near 80F degrees are forecast overnight. 

Friday-Sunday... A persistent forecast is expected with drier air
in the mid to upper levels expected to keep rain chances below
normal through the weekend. Model guidance is in good agreement
that the mid/upper level ridge will build over the Gulf and
eastern CONUS through Sunday before shifting west-southwest Sunday
evening. Guidance shows 500mb heights reaching the Expect maximum
percentile for this time of year at 598dm. Expect isolated to 
scattered showers (20-40% chance) and lightning storms to develop 
in the afternoon and evening as collisions occur between sea 
breezes and outflow from previous showers/lightning storms before 
rain chances diminish by around 8PM on Friday. Below normal rain 
chances (20-50%) are expected to continue on Saturday with the 
greatest chances across the Treasure Coast to Okeechobee county 
(50%). Light and variable winds will increase into the afternoon 
and evening at 5-10mph near the coast on Sunday. Mostly dry 
conditions are expected on Sunday with a low chance (20-30%) for 
isolated to widely scattered showers and lightning storms forecast
along and north of Lake Kissimmee to Cocoa. Afternoon highs in 
the mid to upper 90s are forecast. Additional heat advisories are 
likely through at least Saturday with heat index values up to 
108-112F degrees forecast. A widespread Moderate to Major HeatRisk
is forecast with a widespread Extreme HeatRisk mainly north of 
the Treasure Coast. A Major and Extreme HeatRisk affect anyone 
without adequate cooling and hydration. 

Monday-Wednesday... Much of the same is forecast through at least
the early part of the week with high pressure still in place over
the Gulf and southern US. Ensembles, LREF-clusters, and
deterministic models are in fairly good agreement that the
mid/upper level ridge will shift west-southwest over the southern
US as a mid/upper trough deepens over the northeastern US. At the
surface, a frontal boundary is forecast to sag over the eastern
CONUS and southern US Tuesday into Wednesday. Below normal rain
chances are forecast to continue, as well as hot and muggy 
conditions. A widespread Major HeatRisk is likely for much of east
central Florida each day. Additionally, the probabilities for an 
Extreme HeatRisk are up to 30-70% over areas mainly north of the 
Treasure Coast each day.
